newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament ratifies Belarus union deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament ratifies Belarus union deal.

text.p: The Federation Council upper house of the Russian parliament ratified a Union Treaty with the neigbouring republic of Belarus on Tuesday.

A total of 144 deputies voted for the treaty and an accompanying charter, which formalise a loose union between the two Slav states signed by Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko last month.
No one voted against and only three abstained.
The State Duma lower house had ratified the documents last Friday.

The deal was a watered-down version of an original draft, amended last month after liberals in the Russian government warned that the original could give hardliner Lukashenko too much power and damage Russia's interests.

The lower house of the Belarussian parliament, created after a controversial referendum last November, unanimously backed the integration deal late last month and the Belarussian upper chamber is due to consider the accord later on Tuesday.
Belarussian opposition activists refuse to recognise the new parliament and are fiercely opposed to the deal, which they say is a sell-out of Belarussian interests.
But most Russians and Belarussians, nostalgic for the Soviet Union, support integration moves between their two states.
